summary: Set up a LUKS2-encrypted volume on node1, backed by a 2GB loop file, mounted at /srv/secure with xfs. Auto-unlock at boot uses a root-only keyfile referenced in /etc/crypttab, with the mount defined in /etc/fstab. Verified via a full node reboot that the volume unlocks and mounts automatically with no manual intervention, and that data survives.
actions_performed: Installed cryptsetup on node1 via dnf
Created a 2GB backing file at /var/lib/secure-vol/srv-secure.img and LUKS2-formatted it with a randomly generated 512-bit keyfile stored at /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/srv-secure.key (mode 400, root:root)
Opened the mapping (srv-secure), created an xfs filesystem, and mounted it at /srv/secure
Added persistent /etc/crypttab entry (keyfile-based auto-unlock, nofail) and /etc/fstab entry (auto-mount, nofail) for the volume
Wrote a marker file into /srv/secure and applied SELinux restorecon to the new filesystem
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and healthy mounted state
Issued a native reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1 with the acknowledgement returned before disconnection, then polled until exec access returned

Verified boot_id changed (proving an actual restart), and confirmed systemd-cryptsetup@srv-secure.service and srv-secure.mount were both active post-boot with the marker file content intact, proving unattended unlock and mount at boot

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure
evidence.summary: No spare block device existed on node1 (single vda disk fully partitioned), so a 2GB loop-backed LUKS2 file was created and formatted with xfs; setup script output shows successful luksFormat, mkfs.xfs, and mount at /srv/secure with a test marker file written and readable.

evidence.requirement: Auto-unlock and auto-mount configured for boot (crypttab/fstab)
evidence.summary: Setup script output shows the added /etc/crypttab line (srv-secure image keyfile luks,nofail) and /etc/fstab line (/dev/mapper/srv-secure /srv/secure xfs defaults,nofail) plus a successful systemctl daemon-reload.

Captured boot_id 739c9792-2418-47cc-a875-95b27428f3fc, confirmed /srv/secure mounted with correct marker content, and inspected the generated systemd-cryptsetup unit and srv-secure.mount (active) prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection
evidence.summary: Issued `shutdown -r now` backgrounded via nohup so the exec call returned 'reboot-acknowledged' successfully before the node went down; subsequent exec calls timed out/reset, confirming the node was rebooting.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Polled node1 through connection timeout and reset states until reachable again; the returned boot_id (b9476b96-8a4c-48d2-a25a-835ab74deea1) differs from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a genuine reboot rather than mere elapsed time.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: encrypted volume auto-unlocked, mounted, and data intact without manual action
evidence.summary: Immediately after regaining exec access post-reboot (no manual mount/unlock commands issued), /srv/secure was already a mountpoint, systemd-cryptsetup@srv-secure.service and srv-secure.mount were both 'active', df showed the mapped xfs filesystem, and the marker file content matched exactly what was written before reboot.
